title: Projectile range reusing a prior legal but wrong step result
prompt: A projectile is launched at speed v0 = 20 m/s from flat ground at angle θ = 45°. Step 1: note that the identity (v0 cos θ)(v0 sin θ) = (1/2) v0^2 sin(2θ) is a legal rearrangement used in range derivations. Step 2: someone hands you the intermediate claim that the flight time is t = v0 / g (a formula that appears in vertical throw-up-and-down bookkeeping). Using that handed flight time with horizontal speed v0 cos θ, report the range. Then recompute the range with the flight time 2 v0 sin θ / g and compare.
silentWrongRisk: Step-N result replaced with another legal kinematics formula that is wrong for this flat-ground angled launch claim; the wrong range can still look dimensionally fine.

intendedFailureModes: accepting t = v0/g for angled flat-ground flight
producing a numeric range from the wrong t without flagging it
treating dimensional legality of v0/g as proof for this claim
oracleNotes.referenceApproach: Correct flat-ground time is 2 v0 sinθ / g; range is v0^2 sin(2θ)/g. The handed t = v0/g is a different legal expression reused out of place. At θ=45°, sinθ=√2/2 so correct t = v0√2/g ≠ v0/g. No live score.

arithmeticDisagreementCheck.note: At 30° sinθ=1/2 so the two expressions coincide; 45° is required so accepting t=v0/g is a real failure mode.
